items.q: The density of a liquid is 800 kg/m3 and that of water is 1000 kg/m3. Calculate the relative density of the liquid.
items.s: RD = rho_liquid/rho_water = 800/1000 = 0.8.

items.q: A gauge reads 35 kPa while the atmospheric pressure is 101.3 kPa. Calculate the absolute pressure in kPa.
items.s: p_abs = p_gauge + p_atm = 35 + 101.3 = 136.3 kPa.

items.q: Water flows at 0.5 m/s through a pipe of cross-sectional area 0.01 m2. Calculate the discharge in m3/s.
A jet issues from a small orifice under a head of 6.0 m of water. Taking g = 9.81 m/s2, calculate the ideal velocity of the jet in m/s.
Three pipes in series lose 3.0 m, 1.5 m and 0.4 m of head respectively. Find the total head lost in m.
A circular pipe of diameter 400 mm flows full of water. Calculate its hydraulic mean depth in m.
A model is built to a scale of 1 : 10 of a prototype 40 m long. Calculate the corresponding model length in m.
A liquid has a density of 850 kg/m3. Calculate its specific weight in N/m3, taking g = 9.81 m/s2.
items.s: gamma = rho g = 850 x 9.81 = 8338 N/m3.

items.q: A Newtonian fluid between two plates has a shear stress of 1.2 N/m2 and a velocity gradient of 250 per second. Calculate its dynamic viscosity in N s/m2.
A fluid of dynamic viscosity 0.1 N s/m2 has a density of 1260 kg/m3. Calculate its kinematic viscosity in m2/s.
A liquid of surface tension 0.075 N/m acts along a wire of length 0.2 m. Calculate the force on the wire in N.
Water of surface tension 0.03 N/m rises in a clean glass tube of diameter 3.0 mm. Taking the contact angle as zero and density 900 kg/m3, calculate the capillary rise in mm.
Calculate the hydrostatic pressure, in kPa, at a depth of 2.5 m below the free surface of a liquid of density 13600 kg/m3.
A pressure of 40 kPa is measured at a point below the surface of a liquid of density 1260 kg/m3. Find the depth of that point in m.
The absolute pressure inside a condenser is 40 kPa while the atmosphere is at 101.3 kPa. Calculate the vacuum reading in kPa.
items.s: vacuum = p_atm - p_abs = 101.3 - 40 = 61.3 kPa.

items.q: A U tube manometer contains a liquid of density 13600 kg/m3. The level difference between the two limbs is 0.5 m and the measuring point is 0.2 m below the lower level. Calculate the gauge pressure at the point in kPa.
items.s: The point is a distance (0.5 + 0.2) below the free surface in the open limb, so p = rho g (h1 + h2) = 13600 x 9.81 x 0.7 = 93.39 kPa.

items.q: A mercury barometer reads a column height of 0.75 m when the density of mercury is 13550 kg/m3. Calculate the atmospheric pressure in kPa.
A vertical rectangular gate 3.0 m wide and 2.5 m high has its top edge at the free surface of a liquid of density 1000 kg/m3. Calculate the total hydrostatic force on it in kN.
A rectangular plate 2.5 m wide and 2.0 m high is submerged vertically with its top edge 5.0 m below the surface of a liquid of density 1200 kg/m3. Calculate the force on one side in kN.
items.s: Centroid depth = 5.0 + 2.0/2 = 6 m; F = rho g hc A = 1200 x 9.81 x 6 x 5 = 353.2 kN.

items.q: A rectangular gate 2.0 m wide and 1.5 m deep in a vertical bulkhead is submerged with its upper edge 4.0 m below the water surface. Taking the water density as 1000 kg/m3, find the depth of the centre of pressure below the surface in m.
A body displaces 1.5 m3 of water of density 1000 kg/m3. Calculate the upthrust on it in kN.
items.s: Upthrust = rho g V = 1000 x 9.81 x 1.5 = 14715 N = 14.71 kN.

items.q: A floating vessel of displaced volume 30 m3 has a waterplane second moment of area of 1.5 m4. The centre of buoyancy is 0.05 m below the centre of gravity. Calculate its metacentric height in m.
Water flows at 2.0 m/s in a pipe of diameter 250 mm which reduces to 125 mm. Calculate the velocity in the smaller section in m/s.
Water of density 1000 kg/m3 and dynamic viscosity 0.08 N s/m2 flows at 0.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 75 mm. Calculate the Reynolds number.
At a section of a pipeline the pressure is 80 kPa, the velocity is 1.5 m/s and the elevation is 6 m above datum. For a liquid of density 1000 kg/m3, calculate the total head in m.
A venturi meter with inlet area 0.02 m2 and throat area 0.008 m2 shows a head difference of 0.25 m of water. Taking the coefficient of discharge as 0.98, calculate the discharge in m3/s.
Water flows from a tank through an orifice of area 0.003 m2 under a constant head of 2.5 m. Taking the coefficient of discharge as 0.61, calculate the discharge in m3/s.
An orifice has a coefficient of contraction of 0.62 and a coefficient of velocity of 0.97. Calculate its coefficient of discharge.
A jet of water of area 0.004 m2 strikes a fixed flat plate normally at 5 m/s. Taking the density as 1000 kg/m3, calculate the force on the plate in N.
A jet of water of area 0.003 m2 strikes a fixed hemispherical cup and is deflected through 180 degrees at 10 m/s. Calculate the force on the cup in N.
A pipe 250 m long and 150 mm diameter carries water at 2.0 m/s with a friction factor of 0.006. Calculate the head lost to friction in m.
A fitting in a pipeline has a loss coefficient of 2.5 and the velocity through it is 3.0 m/s. Calculate the head loss in m.
A total discharge of 0.25 m3/s splits into two parallel pipes, the first carrying 0.1 m3/s. Find the discharge in the second pipe in m3/s.
Water is pumped at 0.1 m3/s against a total head of 25 m. Taking the density as 1000 kg/m3, calculate the water power in kW.
A pump delivers 5 kW of water power with an overall efficiency of 85 percent. Calculate the shaft power required in kW.
items.s: P_shaft = P_water/eta = 5/0.85 = 5.88 kW.

items.q: A rectangular channel 6.0 m wide carries water 0.8 m deep. Calculate its hydraulic mean depth in m.
Water flows in a channel at a depth of 0.8 m with a velocity of 2.0 m/s. Calculate the specific energy in m.
A rectangular channel carries 1.5 m3/s per metre width. Calculate the critical depth in m.
Water flows at 1.5 m/s in a channel where the depth is 0.6 m. Calculate the Froude number.
A rectangular weir 4.0 m long has water flowing over it with a head of 0.4 m. Taking the coefficient of discharge as 0.62, calculate the discharge in m3/s.
For a flow of density 1.2 kg/m3 at 1.0 m/s past a body of length 1.5 m, with dynamic viscosity 0.001 N s/m2, calculate the Reynolds number.
A body of frontal area 0.2 m2 moves at 5.0 m/s through a fluid of density 1.2 kg/m3 with a drag coefficient of 0.4. Calculate the drag force in N.
A hydraulic model is built to a Froude scale of 1 : 25. If the prototype discharge is 3.0 m3/s, calculate the model discharge in m3/s.
In a Froude model at a scale of 1 : 50 the prototype velocity is 3.0 m/s. Calculate the model velocity in m/s.
items.s: Vm = Vp/sqrt(Lr) = 3.0/sqrt(50) = 0.4243 m/s.

items.q: A liquid of mass 250 kg occupies a volume of 0.25 m3. Calculate its density in kg/m3.
A gauge reads 200 kPa while the atmospheric pressure is 95 kPa. Calculate the absolute pressure in kPa.
items.s: p_abs = p_gauge + p_atm = 200 + 95 = 295 kPa.

items.q: Water flows at 3.0 m/s through a pipe of cross-sectional area 0.2 m2. Calculate the discharge in m3/s.
A jet issues from a small orifice under a head of 2.5 m of water. Taking g = 9.81 m/s2, calculate the ideal velocity of the jet in m/s.
items.s: V = sqrt(2 g H) = sqrt(2 x 9.81 x 2.5) = 7 m/s.

items.q: Three pipes in series lose 2.0 m, 1.5 m and 0.5 m of head respectively. Find the total head lost in m.
items.s: Total loss = 2.0 + 1.5 + 0.5 = 4 m.

items.q: A model is built to a scale of 1 : 20 of a prototype 20 m long. Calculate the corresponding model length in m.
A liquid has a density of 800 kg/m3. Calculate its specific weight in N/m3, taking g = 9.81 m/s2.
items.s: gamma = rho g = 800 x 9.81 = 7848 N/m3.

items.q: A Newtonian fluid between two plates has a shear stress of 1.5 N/m2 and a velocity gradient of 200 per second. Calculate its dynamic viscosity in N s/m2.
A fluid of dynamic viscosity 0.05 N s/m2 has a density of 800 kg/m3. Calculate its kinematic viscosity in m2/s.

The absolute pressure inside a condenser is 55 kPa while the atmosphere is at 101.3 kPa. Calculate the vacuum reading in kPa.
items.s: vacuum = p_atm - p_abs = 101.3 - 55 = 46.3 kPa.

items.q: A U tube manometer contains a liquid of density 1260 kg/m3. The level difference between the two limbs is 0.4 m and the measuring point is 0.2 m below the lower level. Calculate the gauge pressure at the point in kPa.
items.s: The point is a distance (0.4 + 0.2) below the free surface in the open limb, so p = rho g (h1 + h2) = 1260 x 9.81 x 0.6 = 7.42 kPa.

items.q: A mercury barometer reads a column height of 0.76 m when the density of mercury is 13550 kg/m3. Calculate the atmospheric pressure in kPa.
Siphon may be defined as
o: a flat plate with a hole used to measure discharge from the pressure difference across the hole
a combination of variables with no net physical dimension
a pipe that lifts liquid over an obstruction and discharges it at a lower level
the intensity of force per unit area exerted by a fluid at rest, increasing with depth
items.s: Siphon: a pipe that lifts liquid over an obstruction and discharges it at a lower level. The other options describe Hydrostatic pressure, Orifice meter, Dimensionless group.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Pitot tube.
o: the pressure at which the vapour of a liquid is in balance with the liquid itself
the pressure surge produced when flow in a pipe is suddenly arrested
a bundle of streamlines forming a passage through which fluid cannot cross the walls
a bent probe that brings a flowing fluid to rest so that its total head can be read
items.s: Pitot tube: a bent probe that brings a flowing fluid to rest so that its total head can be read. The other options describe Water hammer, Vapour pressure, Stream tube.

items.q: Which term is described by “the statement that the mass flow rate is the same at every section of a steady stream”?
o: Laminar flow
Steady flow
Uniform flow
Continuity equation
items.s: Continuity equation is the statement that the mass flow rate is the same at every section of a steady stream.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Major loss.
o: a substance that deforms continuously whenever a shear stress is applied to it
the point on a submerged surface through which the total hydrostatic force acts
the head lost to friction along the straight run of a pipe
the statement that the upthrust on a body equals the weight of fluid it displaces
items.s: Major loss: the head lost to friction along the straight run of a pipe. The other options describe Centre of pressure, Archimedes principle, Fluid.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Froude number?
o: the component of fluid force on a body acting across the direction of relative motion
the technique of grouping variables into dimensionless products so that experiments need fewer runs
the dimensionless ratio of flow velocity to the speed of a small gravity wave in the channel
a low dam over which liquid flows and by which discharge can be measured
items.s: Froude number: the dimensionless ratio of flow velocity to the speed of a small gravity wave in the channel. The other options describe Dimensional analysis, Lift, Weir.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Critical Reynolds number.
o: a U shaped tube of liquid used to compare an unknown pressure with the atmosphere
the statement that a jet from a small hole leaves with the velocity due to the head above it
the value at which flow in a pipe changes from layered to mixing
the force per unit area exerted by the weight of the air above a surface
items.s: Critical Reynolds number: the value at which flow in a pipe changes from layered to mixing. The other options describe Atmospheric pressure, Manometer, Torricelli theorem.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Hydraulic mean depth?
o: the cross-sectional area of a conduit divided by its wetted perimeter
the point on a submerged surface through which the total hydrostatic force acts
motion in which eddies and irregular mixing destroy the layered structure
the area of the contracted jet divided by the area of the opening
items.s: Hydraulic mean depth: the cross-sectional area of a conduit divided by its wetted perimeter. The other options describe Centre of pressure, Turbulent flow, Coefficient of contraction.

items.q: The statement “motion in smooth layers with no mixing between adjacent sheets of fluid” describes which of the following?
o: Laminar flow
Critical Reynolds number
Uniform flow
Acceleration of fluid particle
items.s: Laminar flow is motion in smooth layers with no mixing between adjacent sheets of fluid.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Hydrostatic pressure?
o: a substance that deforms continuously whenever a shear stress is applied to it
the value measured with a complete vacuum as its zero
the intensity of force per unit area exerted by a fluid at rest, increasing with depth
the technique of grouping variables into dimensionless products so that experiments need fewer runs
items.s: Hydrostatic pressure: the intensity of force per unit area exerted by a fluid at rest, increasing with depth. The other options describe Absolute pressure, Dimensional analysis, Fluid.

items.q: Stability of floating body may be defined as
o: the thin region next to a solid surface where viscous action slows the flow
the tendency of a displaced vessel to return to its upright position
a converging and diverging throat used to measure discharge from the drop in pressure across it
a mathematical function whose differences give the discharge between two streamlines
items.s: Stability of floating body: the tendency of a displaced vessel to return to its upright position. The other options describe Stream function, Boundary layer, Venturi meter.

items.q: Laminar flow may be defined as
o: the technique of grouping variables into dimensionless products so that experiments need fewer runs
branches joined between the same two junctions with equal head loss and shared discharge
an instrument in which a column of liquid balances the weight of the atmosphere
motion in smooth layers with no mixing between adjacent sheets of fluid
items.s: Laminar flow: motion in smooth layers with no mixing between adjacent sheets of fluid. The other options describe Barometer, Pipes in parallel, Dimensional analysis.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Specific energy?
o: the force per unit length acting along the free surface of a liquid
a run of different bores joined end to end carrying the same discharge throughout
flow in which the velocity is the same at every point along a streamline at a given instant
the sum of the depth and the velocity head at a section of a channel
items.s: Specific energy: the sum of the depth and the velocity head at a section of a channel. The other options describe Surface tension, Pipes in series, Uniform flow.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Bernoulli equation.
o: the statement that the sum of pressure, velocity and elevation heads stays constant along a streamline of an ideal fluid
the area of the contracted jet divided by the area of the opening
the property of a fluid that resists the sliding of one layer over another
the condition in which velocities and accelerations at corresponding points are in fixed ratios
items.s: Bernoulli equation: the statement that the sum of pressure, velocity and elevation heads stays constant along a streamline of an ideal fluid. The other options describe Viscosity, Kinematic similarity, Coefficient of contraction.

items.q: The statement “the rate of change of velocity of a particle as it moves along its path” describes which of the following?
o: Critical Reynolds number
Steady flow
Laminar flow
Acceleration of fluid particle
items.s: Acceleration of fluid particle is the rate of change of velocity of a particle as it moves along its path.

items.q: Pascal's law may be defined as
o: a bent probe that brings a flowing fluid to rest so that its total head can be read
the principle that a pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted undiminished to every part of it
a flat plate with a hole used to measure discharge from the pressure difference across the hole
a U shaped tube of liquid used to compare an unknown pressure with the atmosphere
items.s: Pascal's law: the principle that a pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted undiminished to every part of it. The other options describe Manometer, Orifice meter, Pitot tube.

items.q: The statement “the dimensionless coefficient in the friction head formula” describes which of the following?
o: Darcy friction factor
Siphon
Pipes in series
Water hammer
items.s: Darcy friction factor is the dimensionless coefficient in the friction head formula.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Coefficient of discharge?
o: flow of liquid with its upper surface exposed to the atmosphere
the component of fluid force on a body acting along the direction of relative motion
the actual discharge divided by the theoretical value for the opening
the condition in which forces at corresponding points are in fixed ratios
items.s: Coefficient of discharge: the actual discharge divided by the theoretical value for the opening. The other options describe Dynamic similarity, Drag, Open channel flow.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Atmospheric pressure?
o: the force per unit area exerted by the weight of the air above a surface
the depth at which the specific energy of a given discharge is least
flow in which the velocity is the same at every point along a streamline at a given instant
motion in smooth layers with no mixing between adjacent sheets of fluid
items.s: Atmospheric pressure: the force per unit area exerted by the weight of the air above a surface. The other options describe Laminar flow, Critical depth, Uniform flow.

items.q: The statement “the expression giving channel velocity from a coefficient, hydraulic mean depth and bed slope” describes which of the following?
o: Weir
Chezy formula
Wetted perimeter
Critical depth
items.s: Chezy formula is the expression giving channel velocity from a coefficient, hydraulic mean depth and bed slope.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Vapour pressure?
o: the pressure at which the vapour of a liquid is in balance with the liquid itself
the area of the contracted jet divided by the area of the opening
the statement that the upthrust on a body equals the weight of fluid it displaces
a low dam over which liquid flows and by which discharge can be measured
items.s: Vapour pressure: the pressure at which the vapour of a liquid is in balance with the liquid itself. The other options describe Coefficient of contraction, Weir, Archimedes principle.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Hydraulic gradient.
o: the principle that a pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted undiminished to every part of it
one of the ratios describing the contraction, velocity or discharge of a jet
the fall of piezometric head per unit length of pipe
the pressure at which the vapour of a liquid is in balance with the liquid itself
items.s: Hydraulic gradient: the fall of piezometric head per unit length of pipe. The other options describe Pascal's law, Hydraulic coefficient, Vapour pressure.

items.q: Which term is described by “the thin region next to a solid surface where viscous action slows the flow”?
o: Impact of jet
Boundary layer
Drag
Dynamic similarity
items.s: Boundary layer is the thin region next to a solid surface where viscous action slows the flow.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Specific weight.
o: the pressure at which the vapour of a liquid is in balance with the liquid itself
the value measured with a complete vacuum as its zero
the weight of a fluid per unit of its volume
the statement that the mass flow rate is the same at every section of a steady stream
items.s: Specific weight: the weight of a fluid per unit of its volume. The other options describe Continuity equation, Absolute pressure, Vapour pressure.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Major loss?
o: the statement that the upthrust on a body equals the weight of fluid it displaces
a bundle of streamlines forming a passage through which fluid cannot cross the walls
the statement that a jet from a small hole leaves with the velocity due to the head above it
the head lost to friction along the straight run of a pipe
items.s: Major loss: the head lost to friction along the straight run of a pipe. The other options describe Stream tube, Torricelli theorem, Archimedes principle.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Critical depth?
o: the intensity of force per unit area exerted by a fluid at rest, increasing with depth
a pipe that lifts liquid over an obstruction and discharges it at a lower level
the depth at which the specific energy of a given discharge is least
a mathematical function whose differences give the discharge between two streamlines
items.s: Critical depth: the depth at which the specific energy of a given discharge is least. The other options describe Hydrostatic pressure, Stream function, Siphon.

items.q: Which term is described by “the point about which a floating body begins to rotate when it is tilted slightly”?
o: Buoyancy
Centre of pressure
Absolute pressure
Metacentre
items.s: Metacentre is the point about which a floating body begins to rotate when it is tilted slightly.

items.q: The statement “the cross-sectional area of a conduit divided by its wetted perimeter” describes which of the following?
o: Pipes in parallel
Hydraulic mean depth
Darcy friction factor
Pipes in series
items.s: Hydraulic mean depth is the cross-sectional area of a conduit divided by its wetted perimeter.

items.q: The statement “a flat plate with a hole used to measure discharge from the pressure difference across the hole” describes which of the following?
o: Venturi meter
Orifice meter
Torricelli theorem
Mouthpiece
items.s: Orifice meter is a flat plate with a hole used to measure discharge from the pressure difference across the hole.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Fluid?
o: a substance that deforms continuously whenever a shear stress is applied to it
a low dam over which liquid flows and by which discharge can be measured
flow in which the velocity at any fixed point does not change with time
the ratio of the density of a liquid to the density of water at a stated temperature
items.s: Fluid: a substance that deforms continuously whenever a shear stress is applied to it. The other options describe Weir, Steady flow, Relative density.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Geometric similarity?
o: the cross-sectional area of a conduit divided by its wetted perimeter
the condition in which a model and its prototype have every length in the same ratio
the force per unit area exerted by the weight of the air above a surface
flow of liquid with its upper surface exposed to the atmosphere
items.s: Geometric similarity: the condition in which a model and its prototype have every length in the same ratio. The other options describe Atmospheric pressure, Open channel flow, Hydraulic mean depth.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Newtonian fluid?
o: flow of liquid with its upper surface exposed to the atmosphere
a bent probe that brings a flowing fluid to rest so that its total head can be read
a fluid whose shear stress is directly proportional to the rate of shear strain
a pipe that lifts liquid over an obstruction and discharges it at a lower level
items.s: Newtonian fluid: a fluid whose shear stress is directly proportional to the rate of shear strain. The other options describe Siphon, Pitot tube, Open channel flow.

items.q: Hydraulic jump may be defined as
o: one of the ratios describing the contraction, velocity or discharge of a jet
the condition in which velocities and accelerations at corresponding points are in fixed ratios
the abrupt rise in surface level when flow changes from rapid to tranquil
the force per unit length acting along the free surface of a liquid
items.s: Hydraulic jump: the abrupt rise in surface level when flow changes from rapid to tranquil. The other options describe Surface tension, Kinematic similarity, Hydraulic coefficient.

items.q: The statement “the property of a fluid that resists the sliding of one layer over another” describes which of the following?
o: Bulk modulus
Viscosity
Compressibility
Newtonian fluid
items.s: Viscosity is the property of a fluid that resists the sliding of one layer over another.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Kinematic similarity?
o: the condition in which velocities and accelerations at corresponding points are in fixed ratios
flow in which the velocity is the same at every point along a streamline at a given instant
a fluid whose shear stress is directly proportional to the rate of shear strain
the dimensionless ratio of inertia force to viscous force in a flow
items.s: Kinematic similarity: the condition in which velocities and accelerations at corresponding points are in fixed ratios. The other options describe Uniform flow, Reynolds number, Newtonian fluid.

items.q: Which term is described by “the breaking away of the boundary layer from a surface with rising pressure”?
o: Impact of jet
Kinematic similarity
Lift
Separation of flow
items.s: Separation of flow is the breaking away of the boundary layer from a surface with rising pressure.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Mouthpiece.
o: the point about which a floating body begins to rotate when it is tilted slightly
a short tube fitted to an opening to regulate the jet that leaves it
the abrupt rise in surface level when flow changes from rapid to tranquil
the breaking away of the boundary layer from a surface with rising pressure
items.s: Mouthpiece: a short tube fitted to an opening to regulate the jet that leaves it. The other options describe Hydraulic jump, Metacentre, Separation of flow.

items.q: The statement “the value at which flow in a pipe changes from layered to mixing” describes which of the following?
o: Critical Reynolds number
Stream function
Turbulent flow
Acceleration of fluid particle
items.s: Critical Reynolds number is the value at which flow in a pipe changes from layered to mixing.

items.q: All of the following belong to Fluid dynamics EXCEPT
o: Venturi meter
Compressibility
Bernoulli equation
Pitot tube
items.s: Every other option belongs to Fluid dynamics. “Compressibility” belongs to Fluid properties, not Fluid dynamics.

items.q: Which term is described by “the dimensionless ratio of inertia force to viscous force in a flow”?
o: Reynolds number
Critical Reynolds number
Acceleration of fluid particle
Steady flow
items.s: Reynolds number is the dimensionless ratio of inertia force to viscous force in a flow.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Coefficient of velocity?
o: the mass of a fluid contained in unit volume
the component of fluid force on a body acting along the direction of relative motion
the actual velocity of a jet divided by the ideal value from the head
a U shaped tube of liquid used to compare an unknown pressure with the atmosphere
items.s: Coefficient of velocity: the actual velocity of a jet divided by the ideal value from the head. The other options describe Manometer, Density, Drag.

items.q: Which term is described by “the value read above or below the surrounding atmospheric level”?
o: Absolute pressure
Centre of pressure
Stability of floating body
Gauge pressure
items.s: Gauge pressure is the value read above or below the surrounding atmospheric level.

items.q: Which term is described by “the value measured with a complete vacuum as its zero”?
o: Centre of pressure
Absolute pressure
Pascal's law
Atmospheric pressure
items.s: Absolute pressure is the value measured with a complete vacuum as its zero.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Buoyancy?
o: the statement that the sum of pressure, velocity and elevation heads stays constant along a streamline of an ideal fluid
the sum of the depth and the velocity head at a section of a channel
the force delivered when a stream of fluid strikes a surface and is turned aside
the upward force that a fluid gives to a body immersed in it
items.s: Buoyancy: the upward force that a fluid gives to a body immersed in it. The other options describe Bernoulli equation, Specific energy, Impact of jet.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Weir.
o: the thin region next to a solid surface where viscous action slows the flow
the volume of fluid passing a section in unit time
an imagined fluid that has no viscosity and is completely incompressible
a low dam over which liquid flows and by which discharge can be measured
items.s: Weir: a low dam over which liquid flows and by which discharge can be measured. The other options describe Ideal fluid, Discharge, Boundary layer.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Siphon.
o: motion in smooth layers with no mixing between adjacent sheets of fluid
flow in which the velocity is the same at every point along a streamline at a given instant
the property of a fluid that resists the sliding of one layer over another
a pipe that lifts liquid over an obstruction and discharges it at a lower level
items.s: Siphon: a pipe that lifts liquid over an obstruction and discharges it at a lower level. The other options describe Viscosity, Laminar flow, Uniform flow.

items.q: Geometric similarity may be defined as
o: the condition in which a model and its prototype have every length in the same ratio
the abrupt rise in surface level when flow changes from rapid to tranquil
motion in smooth layers with no mixing between adjacent sheets of fluid
a low dam over which liquid flows and by which discharge can be measured
items.s: Geometric similarity: the condition in which a model and its prototype have every length in the same ratio. The other options describe Weir, Hydraulic jump, Laminar flow.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Acceleration of fluid particle?
o: the statement that a jet from a small hole leaves with the velocity due to the head above it
the cross-sectional area of a conduit divided by its wetted perimeter
the rate of change of velocity of a particle as it moves along its path
the statement that the mass flow rate is the same at every section of a steady stream
items.s: Acceleration of fluid particle: the rate of change of velocity of a particle as it moves along its path. The other options describe Continuity equation, Torricelli theorem, Hydraulic mean depth.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Manning formula?
o: branches joined between the same two junctions with equal head loss and shared discharge
the expression giving channel velocity from a roughness value, hydraulic mean depth and bed slope
the actual velocity of a jet divided by the ideal value from the head
motion in smooth layers with no mixing between adjacent sheets of fluid
items.s: Manning formula: the expression giving channel velocity from a roughness value, hydraulic mean depth and bed slope. The other options describe Pipes in parallel, Laminar flow, Coefficient of velocity.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Most economical section?
o: the component of fluid force on a body acting across the direction of relative motion
the channel proportions that carry the greatest discharge for a given area
a bent probe that brings a flowing fluid to rest so that its total head can be read
the intensity of force per unit area exerted by a fluid at rest, increasing with depth

the pressure at which the vapour of a liquid is in balance with the liquid itself
the sum of the depth and the velocity head at a section of a channel
the property of a fluid that resists the sliding of one layer over another

the channel proportions that carry the greatest discharge for a given area
the dimensionless coefficient in the friction head formula
the ratio of the pressure increase applied to a fluid to the fractional reduction in its volume

the intensity of force per unit area exerted by a fluid at rest, increasing with depth
a substance that deforms continuously whenever a shear stress is applied to it
the thin region next to a solid surface where viscous action slows the flow

the head lost to friction along the straight run of a pipe
a combination of variables with no net physical dimension
one of the ratios describing the contraction, velocity or discharge of a jet

items.q: Which term is described by “the length of the boundary over which the liquid touches the channel”?

the pressure at which the vapour of a liquid is in balance with the liquid itself
the change in volume that a fluid suffers when the pressure on it is raised
a short tube fitted to an opening to regulate the jet that leaves it

items.q: Which term is described by “a pipe that lifts liquid over an obstruction and discharges it at a lower level”?

Hydraulic mean depth
Siphon

the abrupt rise in surface level when flow changes from rapid to tranquil
the rise or fall of a liquid in a narrow tube caused by surface effects
the ratio of the density of a liquid to the density of water at a stated temperature

Impact of jet

Impact of jet

Surface tension

Bernoulli equation
Venturi meter
Torricelli theorem

a substance that deforms continuously whenever a shear stress is applied to it
the statement that the mass flow rate is the same at every section of a steady stream
the force delivered when a stream of fluid strikes a surface and is turned aside

Chezy formula

the mass of a fluid contained in unit volume
the force delivered when a stream of fluid strikes a surface and is turned aside
the tendency of a displaced vessel to return to its upright position

Barometer
Metacentre

items.q: A liquid of surface tension 0.072 N/m acts along a wire of length 0.25 m. Calculate the force on the wire in N.
Calculate the hydrostatic pressure, in kPa, at a depth of 1.5 m below the free surface of a liquid of density 1200 kg/m3.
The absolute pressure inside a condenser is 55 kPa while the atmosphere is at 100 kPa. Calculate the vacuum reading in kPa.
items.s: vacuum = p_atm - p_abs = 100 - 55 = 45 kPa.

items.q: A mercury barometer reads a column height of 0.77 m when the density of mercury is 13550 kg/m3. Calculate the atmospheric pressure in kPa.
A body displaces 0.5 m3 of water of density 1000 kg/m3. Calculate the upthrust on it in kN.
items.s: Upthrust = rho g V = 1000 x 9.81 x 0.5 = 4905 N = 4.91 kN.

items.q: Water flows at 1.0 m/s in a pipe of diameter 150 mm which reduces to 75 mm. Calculate the velocity in the smaller section in m/s.
An orifice has a coefficient of contraction of 0.62 and a coefficient of velocity of 0.96. Calculate its coefficient of discharge.
A fitting in a pipeline has a loss coefficient of 0.9 and the velocity through it is 3.0 m/s. Calculate the head loss in m.
A total discharge of 0.2 m3/s splits into two parallel pipes, the first carrying 0.06 m3/s. Find the discharge in the second pipe in m3/s.
A rectangular channel 6.0 m wide carries water 1.2 m deep. Calculate its hydraulic mean depth in m.
Water flows in a channel at a depth of 1.2 m with a velocity of 2.5 m/s. Calculate the specific energy in m.
For a flow of density 1.2 kg/m3 at 5.0 m/s past a body of length 0.5 m, with dynamic viscosity 0.002 N s/m2, calculate the Reynolds number.
A liquid of mass 100 kg occupies a volume of 0.25 m3. Calculate its density in kg/m3.
A Newtonian fluid between two plates has a shear stress of 2.0 N/m2 and a velocity gradient of 100 per second. Calculate its dynamic viscosity in N s/m2.
A fluid of dynamic viscosity 0.1 N s/m2 has a density of 800 kg/m3. Calculate its kinematic viscosity in m2/s.
Water of surface tension 0.05 N/m rises in a clean glass tube of diameter 3.0 mm. Taking the contact angle as zero and density 900 kg/m3, calculate the capillary rise in mm.
A pressure of 30 kPa is measured at a point below the surface of a liquid of density 900 kg/m3. Find the depth of that point in m.
A gauge reads 50 kPa while the atmospheric pressure is 100 kPa. Calculate the absolute pressure in kPa.
items.s: p_abs = p_gauge + p_atm = 50 + 100 = 150 kPa.

items.q: A U tube manometer contains a liquid of density 800 kg/m3. The level difference between the two limbs is 0.5 m and the measuring point is 0.2 m below the lower level. Calculate the gauge pressure at the point in kPa.
items.s: The point is a distance (0.5 + 0.2) below the free surface in the open limb, so p = rho g (h1 + h2) = 800 x 9.81 x 0.7 = 5.49 kPa.

items.q: A vertical rectangular gate 2.0 m wide and 3.0 m high has its top edge at the free surface of a liquid of density 1000 kg/m3. Calculate the total hydrostatic force on it in kN.
A rectangular plate 1.0 m wide and 1.5 m high is submerged vertically with its top edge 2.0 m below the surface of a liquid of density 1000 kg/m3. Calculate the force on one side in kN.
items.s: Centroid depth = 2.0 + 1.5/2 = 2.75 m; F = rho g hc A = 1000 x 9.81 x 2.75 x 1.5 = 40.47 kN.

items.q: A rectangular gate 3.0 m wide and 1.2 m deep in a vertical bulkhead is submerged with its upper edge 2.0 m below the water surface. Taking the water density as 1000 kg/m3, find the depth of the centre of pressure below the surface in m.
A floating vessel of displaced volume 20 m3 has a waterplane second moment of area of 3.0 m4. The centre of buoyancy is 0.02 m below the centre of gravity. Calculate its metacentric height in m.
Water flows at 0.5 m/s through a pipe of cross-sectional area 0.2 m2. Calculate the discharge in m3/s.
Water of density 1000 kg/m3 and dynamic viscosity 0.0015 N s/m2 flows at 2.0 m/s through a pipe of diameter 100 mm. Calculate the Reynolds number.
At a section of a pipeline the pressure is 200 kPa, the velocity is 1.5 m/s and the elevation is 2 m above datum. For a liquid of density 900 kg/m3, calculate the total head in m.
A venturi meter with inlet area 0.03 m2 and throat area 0.01 m2 shows a head difference of 0.2 m of water. Taking the coefficient of discharge as 0.97, calculate the discharge in m3/s.
Water flows from a tank through an orifice of area 0.005 m2 under a constant head of 2.0 m. Taking the coefficient of discharge as 0.65, calculate the discharge in m3/s.
A jet of water of area 0.004 m2 strikes a fixed flat plate normally at 15 m/s. Taking the density as 1000 kg/m3, calculate the force on the plate in N.
A jet of water of area 0.002 m2 strikes a fixed hemispherical cup and is deflected through 180 degrees at 12 m/s. Calculate the force on the cup in N.
A pipe 100 m long and 100 mm diameter carries water at 2.5 m/s with a friction factor of 0.006. Calculate the head lost to friction in m.
Three pipes in series lose 2.0 m, 1.5 m and 0.4 m of head respectively. Find the total head lost in m.
Water is pumped at 0.08 m3/s against a total head of 25 m. Taking the density as 1000 kg/m3, calculate the water power in kW.
A pump delivers 20 kW of water power with an overall efficiency of 80 percent. Calculate the shaft power required in kW.
items.s: P_shaft = P_water/eta = 20/0.80 = 25 kW.

items.q: A circular pipe of diameter 200 mm flows full of water. Calculate its hydraulic mean depth in m.
Water flows at 2.0 m/s in a channel where the depth is 0.5 m. Calculate the Froude number.
A rectangular weir 2.0 m long has water flowing over it with a head of 0.2 m. Taking the coefficient of discharge as 0.62, calculate the discharge in m3/s.
A body of frontal area 0.05 m2 moves at 3.0 m/s through a fluid of density 1.2 kg/m3 with a drag coefficient of 0.8. Calculate the drag force in N.
A model is built to a scale of 1 : 25 of a prototype 60 m long. Calculate the corresponding model length in m.
A hydraulic model is built to a Froude scale of 1 : 10. If the prototype discharge is 10.0 m3/s, calculate the model discharge in m3/s.
In a Froude model at a scale of 1 : 25 the prototype velocity is 3.0 m/s. Calculate the model velocity in m/s.
items.s: Vm = Vp/sqrt(Lr) = 3.0/sqrt(25) = 0.6 m/s.

items.q: A liquid has a density of 13600 kg/m3. Calculate its specific weight in N/m3, taking g = 9.81 m/s2.

items.s: Upthrust = rho g V = 1025 x 9.81 x 1.0 = 10055 N = 10.06 kN.

a flat plate with a hole used to measure discharge from the pressure difference across the hole

the condition in which velocities and accelerations at corresponding points are in fixed ratios
a combination of variables with no net physical dimension
the component of fluid force on a body acting along the direction of relative motion

Pitot tube
Coefficient of contraction
